Article Title: Bangladesh PM likely to visit India as Dhaka presses for Sheikh Hasina's extradition
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman likely to visit India

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions."The government is positive about visits to all countries. But it will depend on the PM's schedule and on how far discussions between the two countries progress," state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam said."The government is busy, and so is the prime minister. If everything fits together, of course there will be a visit to India, a visit to Japan; all the visits will happen," she said, referring to ongoing domestic programmes and upcoming constitutional activities.In April, Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties following more than 18 months of heightened diplomatic tensions.Bangladesh has also sought the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday that India has extended two separate invitations to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman — one for a bilateral visit and another to attend the outreach session of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September."Brics is still a long way off. A lot can happen in a month,” Shama said.Asked whether Rahman’s visit to India could help ease tensions, Shama said direct communication between the leaders of the two governments could provide an opportunity to discuss and resolve outstanding issues."Whenever the heads of two countries talk, there is a chance of resolving many problems. That opportunity is there; it remains," she said.Relations between India and Bangladesh deteriorated sharply after the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus came to power following the fall of Sheikh Hasina’s government in August 2024.Efforts to stabilise ties gained momentum after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, accompanied by foreign secretary Vikram Misri, represented India at Tarique Rahman’s swearing-in ceremony in Dhaka on February 17.Rahman assumed office as prime minister after his party secured a landslide victory in the parliamentary elections.Bangladesh’s current government, led by Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has maintained that Sheikh Hasina must surrender and face the law if she returns to the country.Hasina recently addressed an audio-only virtual press conference from New Delhi, her first public media interaction since fleeing to India on August 5, 2024, amid mass protests.During the virtual press conference, Hasina said she was determined to return to Bangladesh in December to put the country on the "right track" by restoring democracy, despite facing the possibility of imprisonment or a death sentence.India distanced itself from Hasina’s media interaction, clarifying that it had neither played a role in organising the event nor endorsed her remarks concerning the Bangladesh government.
Article Summary: Bangladesh prime minister tarique rahman’s proposed visit to india has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions. In april, bangladesh foreign minister khalilur rahman visited india as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties.

Article Title: 'A moment that tore apart several lives': PM Modi on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
Article Text:
Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people.

NEW DELHI: A day ahead of Independence Day , Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday paid tribute to those affected by the Partition of India, remembering their courage and resilience on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day.He described the day as an occasion to remember those whose lives were upended by Partition, which "tore apart several lives, uprooted families and caused immense suffering."“Today we mark Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. We recall the courage of all those who were impacted by Partition. It was a moment in history that tore apart several lives... families were uprooted, loved ones were lost, and immense suffering was endured,” PM Modi wrote in a post on X.The prime minister said that despite the hardships, those affected rebuilt their lives from scratch, overcame adversity and made significant contributions to the country's progress.“Their life journeys remind us of the strength of the human spirit. May this day deepen our resolve to preserve harmony and brotherhood in our nation and collectively work towards building a Viksit Bharat,” he added.India has observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 since 2021 to honour those who lost their lives or were displaced during the Partition of 1947.India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. However, the birth of two new nations - India and Pakistan - was accompanied by the violent Partition, which left deep and lasting scars on millions of people.Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. Millions were forced to leave their ancestral homes, villages, towns and cities and begin new lives as refugees.The upheaval was accompanied by widespread communal violence and the loss of countless lives, leaving a lasting impact on generations that followed.
Article Summary: Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. India has observed partition horrors remembrance day on august 14 since 2021 to honour those who lost their lives or were displaced during the partition of 1947.

While restoring its own embassy in Kabul last year, India had agreed to the appointment of Taliban diplomats.The development followed a landmark visit by Afghanistan foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi to India that further cemented the relationship.

Article Title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
Article Text:
Nepali PM Balen Shah had raised up the issue of border with India, including Lipulekh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.“The Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives. But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,” Khanal said.He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era. Shah said Nepal had found that “not only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.”India rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said “there is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.” He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land. India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as “neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. ”The issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Persons’ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. “We have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,” Gyawali had said. “We are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.”Khanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements. He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.“Under the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,” Khanal said.He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.
Article Summary: Nepali pm balen shah had raised up the issue of border with india, including lipulekh. India has rejected nepal's claims as “neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence” the issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. The sugauli treaty was agreed between nepal and the british east india company after the anglo-nepalese war.

Article Title: Over 11k Indian workers died in Saudi, UAE each in 2021-25, MEA informs Parliament
Article Text:
Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries

Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025 - over 71% of total recorded deaths. According to figures released by ministry of external affairs (MEA) in Parliament on Thursday, Saudi Arabia topped the list with 11,923 deaths, and the UAE was second with 11,489 fatalities. Kuwait reported 3,890 deaths, Oman 2,457, Qatar 1,548 and Bahrain 1,206 deaths. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.From 2022 onwards, while countries like Bahrain and Qatar registered lower death counts, Saudi Arabia and the UAE recorded upward trends through 2024-2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries, with the UAE alone accounting for 4.5 million Indians.
Article Summary: Saudi arabia and the uae accounted for the vast majority of indian worker fatalities across gulf countries from 2021 to 2025. Approximately 10 million indian nationals reside in the six gcc countries. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.

Article Title: 'PM Modi does not sleep at night, Shah disappeared': Rahul mocks BJP, says India expressing itself
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi stresses on 'expression' at the 'Rachnatmak Congress National Convention', at the Constitution Club, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

Rahul attacks govt over Iran war, China

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday said the party's job was to make India “express itself” and claimed the BJP-led government was increasingly unsettled by people's voices. Speaking at the Ratchnatmak Congress National Convention, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha also took several digs at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah and the RSS.“Our job is very simple and we can drive them crazy...I am telling you, (PM) Narendra Modi does not sleep at night,” Rahul said. Referring to Shah, he added, “You saw (HM) Amit Shah, what did they used to call him? Chanakya? And Sardar Patel... Where has he disappeared? He could not enter Parliament House... Why? Because, for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression...”Gandhi said the Congress would seek to challenge what he described as the BJP's attempt to impose a particular political order on the country.“What was happening at Jantar Mantar is that students want to express themselves. They are in pain, and they want to express themselves, and the government says no.We are going to create order at Jantar Mantar. You cannot express yourselves,” he said.“So their job and their political philosophy is to impose an order on India, an order that benefits them and certain other people. And our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” Gandhi added.He was referring to the protests at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The CJP-led protest ended after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, while opposition parties in Parliament demanded a statement from Home Minister Amit Shah on the alleged police action against protesters.Gandhi also attacked the RSS, saying the organisation did not understand contemporary India. “I can understand if you are fighting the British Empire and suddenly you say, I'm feeling a bit scared. But you're fighting a bunch of jokers. How can you feel scared? You're literally fighting a bunch of jokers, clowns who have no idea about our philosophy, no idea about our history. I can naturally say this about my friends in the RSS. It's obvious to me,” he said.“In fact, it's obvious to most people that these people have no understanding of India. Why? Because somebody who cannot connect with India as it is today cannot understand India. To understand India, you can't understand India 3,000 years ago. You have to understand it today, right now. And to understand it today, the only way to understand it today is to understand its expression,” he added.The LoP also criticised the government's foreign policy, referring to the war in Iran and India's ties with the US, Russia and Iran.“War broke out in Iran. For India—had it recognized its own strength and had its leader been someone like Indira Gandhi—this presented the greatest opportunity in the world,” he said.“What kind of opportunity? Iran was our old friend, America was our friend, and Russia was our friend. We could have stepped up, become relevant, and leveraged these friendships. But what actually happened? Nothing of the sort. Instead, Pakistan stepped in and took our place; Pakistan became the mediator, while India and Modi-ji simply looked on,” Gandhi claimed.He also alleged that the government was suppressing information about India's border situation with China.“Rajnath Singh, Amit Shah, and Narendra Modi have been completely deflated. They are calling up all the media editors, telling them, ‘Don't publish this in your newspapers; suppress the story.’ They are causing direct harm to the country without a second thought,” he alleged.Gandhi further referred to the government's response after the Galwan clash and claimed that India's position had weakened its negotiations with China.“After the Galwan incident, the Prime Minister held a meeting—a Zoom call. He stated that China hadn't taken a single inch of Indian territory. The Army said that our land had been taken. Just think about the message sent to China: Chinese negotiators asked our negotiators, ‘What nonsense are you talking about? Your own Prime Minister said no land was lost.’”He alleged that the government's foreign-policy decisions were ultimately driven by political funding, adding, “And they did all of this solely to finance their political structure, to secure funds from Adani ji.”Rahul also criticised what he described as the government's approach to diplomacy, saying foreign policy could not be reduced to personal relationships between leaders.“I don't know where it came from; this idea got into their heads. I don't know who put it there or where it came from, the idea that foreign policy means hugging politicians,” he said.Recalling an incident from his childhood involving his grandmother and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi said she had returned from an official dinner in the US and told his mother, Sonia Gandhi, that “these Americans take me for a complete fool.”Gandhi said Indira Gandhi had noticed that then-US First Lady Nancy Reagan was wearing a dress of the same colour as her sari.“You aren't just visiting a friend's house. In this role, the Prime Minister of India doesn't engage in mere friendship. They have no interest in friendship; their job is to protect the country,” he said.Read more: Rahul mocks PM; another Congress leader takes Meloni swipe
Article Summary: Congress leader rahul gandhi said the party's job was to make india 'express itself' he claimed the bjp-led government was increasingly unsettled by people's voices. Gandhi also took several digs at prime minister narendra modi, home minister amit shah and the rss.

Article Title: Watch: When gunman tried to assassinate Sukhbir Badal at Golden Temple in 2024

NEW DELHI: Sukhbir Singh Badal’s Thursday attack in Nanded marks the second serious attempt on the Shiromani Akali Dal leader’s life. The SAD leader was also attacked two years ago at the Golden Temple when a gunman opened fire at him while Badal was serving religious punishment at the shrine.On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked at the entrance of the temple, where he was seated in a wheelchair because of his fractured leg, during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds.The footage showed him dressed in a blue sewadar uniform. He was stationed at the temple entrance as part of the punishment pronounced by the Akal Takht over alleged misconduct during his tenure from 2007 to 2017.As Badal sat with a placard around his neck, a man who was later identified as Narayan Singh Chaura approached him and opened fire. The attempt, however, was foiled almost immediately.In the clip, right after the gunman pulled out the weapon, an alert sewadar, believed to be a volunteer associated with an Akali leader, intervened and pushed the assailant’s arm upward as he attempted to fire. The bullet was discharged harmlessly into the air, and the attacker was quickly overpowered by volunteers and others present at the scene.Police personnel stationed at the shrine also moved in and apprehended Chaura on the spot. Confirming the swift response, ADCP Harpal Singh said, “No one was injured in the attack.”It was not long after the attempted attack that other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.Despite the dramatic shooting attempt, Badal remained calm.Still seated in his wheelchair, he continued performing his duties as a sewadar, holding a spear and staying at the temple entrance after the assailant had been detained.In a separate clip, the shooter could be seen being overpowered by the crowd. The people holding the man can be heard asking him his motive for opening fire on the SAD leader.The religious punishment had been announced on December 2, 2024, by Sikh high priests for Badal and other Akali leaders in connection with incidents of sacrilege and the pardon granted to controversial Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. The tankhah was part of a reconciliation process led by Sikh religious authorities to address long-standing grievances within the community.With Wednesday’s attack once again putting security arrangements at the Golden Temple under scrutiny, the earlier firing incident has returned to focus as a reminder that this was not the first time Sukhbir Singh Badal was targeted while performing religious service at Sikhism’s holiest shrine.

NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives."Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.Read also: Red Fort blast: 7,500-page NIA charge sheet alleges ‘Operation Heavenly Hind’ to overthrow govt Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.The group was formed to expand the organisation’s activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Da’esh) affiliates.The report noted that Al-Qaida and ISIL had for years shown interest in developing chemical and biological weapons but had so far failed to overcome the technical challenges involved. It also highlighted the widespread circulation of instructions on producing such agents in online terrorist communities.The report cited material published by ISIL’s English-language Invade magazine in February that included instructions related to botulinum toxin and cyanide. It also noted that ISIL-K had shown particular interest in ricin and circulated instructions on developing the toxin over the previous 12 months.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:
. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: There is little chance of the lok sabha continuing with justice varma’s removal motion. As per article 217(1) of the constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the president’

Article Title: 'Soon in a trash can': Iran mocks Trump's secret getaway via catering truck
Article Text:
Photo mocking Trump posted on X by Iran embassy in South Africa

Iranian state media has mocked US President Donald Trump over the secret aircraft switch that took place during his departure from Turkey last month, portraying the episode as evidence of Washington's fear of Iran's military capabilities.A presenter on Iranian state television described the incident as a new “scandal” for Trump and said it had become a source of humiliation for the US president. The comments came after new details emerged about the security operation during Trump's return from the Nato summit in Ankara.The operation was prompted by what US officials described as a credible threat that the presidential aircraft could be targeted by a shoulder-fired missile. Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to a smaller C-32A government jet, while the larger presidential aircraft left separately with senior administration officials, staff and journalists on board.The New York Times had reported that US intelligence also found that Iranian operatives knew where Trump was staying in Ankara, including the floor of his hotel. Tehran has not officially commented on those allegations or the aircraft switch.The episode quickly became material for Iranian propaganda and social media. Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a meme showing Trump inside a catering box filled with food, alongside a warning that he would “be hidden in a trash can before long”.In a follow up post Iran claimed that, “The one they claimed was hiding in a bunker was martyred in his office. Yet the one who boasted about his massive warships and advanced B-2 bombers ended up fleeing in a food truck.”The catering truck was reportedly used to conceal Trump and a small group of aides as they moved from the presidential aircraft to the smaller jet on July 8.Iranian state media also pointed to the broader symbolism of the incident, with a television presenter arguing that the extraordinary security measures demonstrated the reach of Iran's military power. Tehran has previously rejected US allegations that it was involved in plots against Trump.
Article Summary: Iranian state media has mocked us president donald trump over the secret aircraft switch that took place during his departure from turkey last month. A presenter on iranian state television described the incident as a new “scandal” for trump. Article Title: Engulfed in flames, smoke: 2 killed as Russia hits passenger train with 340 onboard, says Zelenskyy
Article Text:
Train on fire (Video shared by Zelenskyy on X)

Ukraine’s drones hit major Russian refinery

A passenger train with 340 people onboard was attacked in Ukraine's Odesa region on Thursday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed, saying the train's driver and his assistant were killed in the strike.Zelenskyy said a Russian drone struck the locomotive of the passenger train. He said the target was a civilian train and that the operator of the drone could not have been unaware of its nature. The claims have not been independently verified.“Today in the Odesa region, the Russians once again destroyed an ordinary passenger train locomotive with a jet-powered drone. There were 340 people on the train,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X.“As of now, unfortunately, we know that the locomotive engineer and his assistant were killed in the strike,” he added, offering condolences to their families.Zelenskyy also said Russian forces carried out strikes across 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, using more than 130 attack drones.He called for greater air defence support for Ukraine and increased international pressure on Russia, saying stronger action was needed to stop the war.The attack comes amid continued Russian drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, with Odesa and its surrounding region frequently targeted.As the attacks continue from both sides, Ukrainian forces were later reported to have struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Russia’s Bashkortostan overnight, causing a fire, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The facility, located about 1,300 km from Ukraine’s border, is one of Russia’s largest oil refineries and petrochemical complexes.The General Staff said the plant can process up to 74 million barrels of oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel and other petroleum products. “The complex is one of Russia’s largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities,” it said.Bashkortostan Governor Radiy Khabirov said a drone attack wounded two civilians and started a fire in an industrial zone in Salavat. The strike was the fourth major Ukrainian attack on Russian energy infrastructure in three days, according to AP.
Article Summary: Ukrainian president volodymyr zelenskyy says a russian drone struck the locomotive of the passenger train. He said the target was a civilian train and that the operator of the drone could not have been unaware of its nature. He called for greater air defence support for ukraine and increased international pressure on russia.

Article Title: Explosion at Europe's largest port kills one, injures six as investigators probe cause
Article Text:
Blast at Rotterdam petroleum storage facility kills one, injures six during maintenance work

A blast at a petroleum storage facility in the Netherlands' Rotterdam port killed one person and injured six others on Thursday, with authorities investigating the cause of the explosion.The blast occurred at around 11.30 am local time during maintenance work on a storage tank operated by energy commodities trader Gunvor. A company spokesperson described it as an “incident” and said Gunvor was cooperating with authorities.Police said there was no immediate indication of sabotage, but all possible causes were being considered.The explosion took place at the Port of Rotterdam, Europe's largest port and a major centre for oil and fuel imports and storage. The sprawling facility also houses major refineries operated by Shell, BP, ExxonMobil and Vitol.Shell said its operations were unaffected, while the port said its LNG terminals were not hit by the blast. Gas flows at Rotterdam's Gate LNG terminal briefly dipped before becoming volatile, although it was unclear whether that was linked to the explosion or a separate power outage elsewhere in the port.ExxonMobil said a power outage affecting its 191,000-barrel-per-day refinery had been resolved and that operations were normal.Rotterdam Port and local authorities said the outage was unrelated to the blast.The incident is being closely watched because the port is a major energy hub for northwestern Europe. The Gate terminal is one of the region's key LNG import facilities, while Dutch gas storage levels are currently around 40% ahead of the winter heating season.
Article Summary: Blast at rotterdam petroleum storage facility kills one, injures six during maintenance work. Police said there was no immediate indication of sabotage, but all possible causes were being considered. The incident is being closely watched because the port is a major energy hub for northwestern europe.

Article Title: Kylie Kelce gets emotional recalling the miscarriage that made her terrified to try again
Article Text:
Kylie Kelce

Why she keeps returning to this story

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. In early pregnancy, she found herself checking survival odds on a near-weekly basis, and by the later stages of her second trimester, that worry shifted into wondering whether a baby born that day could make it. She's been candid that this obsessive tracking wasn't necessarily a healthy habit, just one that helped her get through it, and one that carried into her later pregnancies too.Kelce didn't have to revisit this topic; she's already raising four young daughters, and the loss happened years ago.But her reasoning for continuing to talk about it is straightforward. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. It's a message that fits her reputation for being unusually direct about hard topics, and one she's now delivered twice, in two different ways, likely for the benefit of anyone quietly sitting with the same fear.

This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and jason decided to try again.
